current_answer: Veda-on-ComfyUI gives a measured project-reported H3 clip-speed improvement, not a live stream: on an RTX 5070, one 5.17-second T2VA job fell from 342.1 to 130.1 seconds. The advertised 7.1× is attention time, while the complete job improved 2.63× and remained about 25 times slower than playback. A different 3060 user saw no apparent gain and poor audio; no matched consumer-GPU accepted-output result or cost exists. Director sessions, Vidu live-feed editing, queued playout, and completed H3 clips still answer different jobs.

catalogue_card.question: Did Veda make H3 live on a consumer GPU?
catalogue_card.text: A project RTX 5070 test cut a 5.17-second H3 clip from 342.1 to 130.1 seconds. Its 7.1× headline times attention only; the full job improved 2.63× and is still offline.

summary: Veda-on-ComfyUI project test: on an RTX 5070 12 GB, a 124-frame 1344×768 H3 T2VA clip took 342.1 seconds with default attention, 230.9 with SageAttention and 130.1 with Veda. The 7.1× number is attention-only; the full-job default-to-Veda ratio is 2.63×.

RAVEN ComfyUI’s 192-frame T2VA test used an H200 constrained to 24.100 GiB free and synthetic conditioning. It sampled eight seconds in 301.30 seconds, with first local fragment at 51.46 seconds. A separate 39-frame real-prompt test used unconstrained H200 VRAM; neither proves full-size real-prompt generation on a physical 24-GiB card.

Tavus describes Griffin-Lite as a full-duplex 720p conversational-video preview. Its reported 320 ms chunks and 0.43 s audio-to-video generator latency are not a customer session; NVIDIA VideoFDB has separate 1,892/2,232 ms median generation/perception timing.

vLLM-Omni merged request-scoped H3 latent-mask editing into its video API on 20 September. Source video/audio and masks can preserve or regenerate regions in a completed job. Its proposed ComfyUI editing node and raw-mask server follow-up remained open at the 4 October check; the pool has not run this route.

An independent project reports a warm FastH3 Preview v1 14.375-second 1344×768/24 fps audio-video clip saved in 13.506 seconds on eight H100 80 GB GPUs. A separate matched eight-H200 stock-versus-patched test reports 23.810 to 14.085 seconds; do not merge those comparisons. No accepted-quality, cold-start, receiver or cost result is available.

TaoMate-H3 reports 14.810 seconds pure DiT and 17.287 seconds to benchmark first playable video for a ten-second 480×864 T2AV job on eight H20 96 GB GPUs. First playable includes video VAE decode and H.264 publication but excludes internal audio preparation. Current CLI output is a final MP4; sustained viewer delivery is unmeasured.

NVIDIA Sol-H3 reports eight-B300 warm medians of 1.653/3.732/6.612 seconds for nominal 5/10/15-second 1344×768 T2VA outputs with audio. Final MP4 encoding, load, and compilation are excluded; continuous streaming and in-session control remain future work. The 11.04× five-second comparison also changes Base H3 from 49 denoiser forwards to a four-forward FastH3 adapter.

Vidu S2-Editing documents a source-fed live editing path: publish video into RTC, subscribe to edited RTC output, and optionally relay it to RTMP. It bills one credit per live second; at a $0.005 standard credit, 3,600 billed seconds imply $18 before delivery costs. No independent viewer-delay or long-session result is available.

vLLM-Omni’s current recipe reports a separate warmed eight-B300 FastH3 Dense T2VA test: a 4.4-second, 1344×768 clip returned as a complete MP4 in 11.7 and 11.8 seconds. Four denoiser evaluations took 2.36–2.37 seconds, so the complete short-clip response was still slower than playback. This is distinct from the previously reported longer FastH3 profile that beat its playback clock.

vLLM-Omni v0.30.0 documents opt-in Ref2VA long-video continuation. Its maintainer reports one 736-frame, 30.667-second original-H3 output on eight B300 GPUs at 1344×768, 24 fps, 50 steps; full wall time and live delivery are not supplied.

Comfy Org reports that the H3 video VAE encode/decode round trip fell from 24.3 to 12.7 seconds on an RTX 5090 at 1344×768, 129 frames after its v0.36.0 update. This is one stage, not whole-job speed.

vLLM-Omni says H3 can admit and retire requests between denoise steps, but its stated two-H100 test with four simultaneous 672×384, 209-frame, 30-step requests reports worse wall time and mean latency under four-way co-batching than ordinary request mode.
The source says staggered-arrival behavior remains unmeasured. The benchmark does not predict two RTX 5090 GPUs, a different job shape, a FastH3 adapter, a browser-visible result, or a public stream.

The current two-RTX-5090 DLO launch selects the FL2VA DiT; T2VA uses that path. The source recommends a 384 GiB host, while its one 50-step T2VA validation returned 124 1344×768 / 24 fps frames in 8 minutes 38 seconds.
vLLM-Omni’s current ComfyUI client still accepts one FL2VA frame even though the server recipe can represent ordered first-and-last-frame inputs.
uncertainty: The Veda benchmark is project-maintained on a specific RTX 5070 T2VA setup; 5090, 3060, reference-input and longer-output quality and complete-job gains are unverified by this pool.
RAVEN physical 24-GiB real-prompt 192-frame fit, viewer delivery, accepted quality and usable cost are unmeasured; maintainer advises 160 GiB available host RAM.
Griffin-Lite is limited to selected research testers; no pool-operated session, Griffin-specific customer price, accepted-quality distribution or delivered-hour bill exists.
The merged H3 mask API has no pool-operated edit, accepted-quality comparison, complete wait, bill, or live receiver result. The client and raw-mask PR states may change after 4 October.

The Hopper FastH3 results are project-reported. Warm complete-MP4 timing excludes load and compilation; quality suite, receiver-visible continuity, retries and billing are unknown. The H100 headline and H200 A/B use different hardware.

TaoMate-H3 figures are project-reported for one eight-H20 480×864 test. No pool test, cold start, internal audio preparation, receiver-visible first frame, repeated-block timing, accepted quality or delivered-hour cost is available.
The one-RTX-5090 converted TaoMate LoRA is a separate self-reported ComfyUI offline path, not validation of the official chunked runtime.
Sol-H3 results are project-reported, not pool-tested; final encoded-to-viewer time, quality acceptance, queue behavior, session reliability and cost are unknown.
Vidu S2 Editing topology and billing are provider-documented; no pool or independent timed RTC-to-RTMP session, billed invoice, viewer latency, or long-run reliability record was found.

The new FastH3 Dense timing is two project-reported warm runs on eight B300 GPUs for one 4.4-second T2VA shape; no pool reproduction, cost, video-quality, queue, first-frame, or viewer result is available.
The vLLM-Omni long-video example is a project-maintained eight-B300 result. The 300-second request cap does not validate five-minute output, acceptable joins, cost, or a stream.

The ComfyUI VAE speed figures are provider-maintained node-level A/B measurements on one RTX 5090 setup. Full H3 render time, quality under a pinned workflow, repeated-run reliability, and cost impact remain unmeasured.
The batching result is one project-maintained two-H100 benchmark with four simultaneous requests. Staggered arrivals, other job shapes, other hardware, and viewer-visible behavior remain unmeasured.
The documented two-RTX-5090 result is one project-published T2VA validation. The pool did not independently audit its environment, media, timing, or quality.

The two-5090 command selects the FL2VA path; it does not establish a combined multi-task service, Ref2VA, a two-keyframe client workflow, warm performance, streaming, queueing, or first visible frame.
vLLM-Omni’s current ComfyUI client-scope statements come from an open RFC. The pool did not install or test the server or client.
Dreamverse’s FastH3 profile is project documentation; the pool did not install or run it, inspect a generated handoff, or measure buffer, cost, recovery, or uptime.
FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on FastH3 8-Step V2 FL2VA scope. The pool did not run a pinned T2VA or FL2VA workflow.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end source-to-visible latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics record is available.
freshness_note: Checked 7 October 2026. Veda shortens one project-tested offline H3 job; 7.1× is attention-only and 130.1 seconds for about 5.17 seconds of video is not live.
